title: fix(auth)!: a boot outside development mode retires what the development seed issued
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X1qGnTYLQs3EtmtCmjrcfCe)_

Fixes #35184

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no skill states what a boot outside development mode does to a seeded account's credentials. `skills/**` names the development seed only as `os dev --seed-admin` (`skills/objectstack-platform/references/operations.md`) and `stack.signIn()` for tests, and `skills/objectstack-platform/evals/config-plugins-ops.json` says production creates no demo account, which stays true; checked at `origin/main`.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：不在开发模式的服务器每次启动、开始接请求之前，会结束开发种子建的管理员和演示账号在开发期拿到的会话、API key 和令牌；只针对仍是种子密码的这些账号，运维改过密码的账号和管理员自建的账号不受影响，开发模式下什么都不变。
- 为什么做：开发种子凭据加固的第三项，即维护者裁决中留作跟进的那一项：离开开发模式后，开发种子签发的东西不再继续起作用。
- 出错会怎样：拿开发库直接上生产的部署，这些账号的旧会话和 key 会失效，需要运维改密后重新登录、重新发 key；结束不干净时服务器拒绝启动并说明是哪些账号；回滚即撤回本 PR，已结束的会话不会恢复，key 可由平台管理员恢复。
- 要你做什么：需要你批准后由席位落地。

## What changes

**The rule (ruling item 3 on #34717, the card's text): when a deployment leaves development mode, nothing the development seed issued keeps acting for an account that carries the development seed stamp.** Development mode is `NODE_ENV=development`, read through the same predicate the refusals of #34717 use (`isDevelopmentMode`). There is no switch, flag or opt-out key.

- **`dev-seed-credential-retirement.ts` (new), `retireDevSeedCredentials`.** Outside development mode it reads the stamped accounts (one indexed read on `sys_user.dev_seed_credential`; a database with none costs that one read), keeps those whose seed credential is still in force (`isDevSeedCredentialInForce`: the stored hash is still the one the seed stored), and for each one retires:
  - through the existing revocation `os user set-password` uses (`revokeSessionsAndApiKeys`): every live session (tombstoned in place, ADR-0069 D4), every admissible API key (`revoked: true`), every app authorized to it and its device sign-ins (read through better-auth's own adapter and plugin registry, as the administrator's forced reset reads them), every linked sign-in account, every OAuth application it registered (disabled) and every SCIM credential it minted (revoked). Sessions and keys carry the existing reason `admin_password_reset`, so a retired key is restored only by a platform administrator;
  - every outstanding password-reset token, rows and cache entries (`endOutstandingResetTokens`);
  - with a host `secondaryStorage` that holds the sessions of record (no `sys_session` row exists then), its sessions there, through better-auth's `deleteUserSessions`, read back after (the vendor logs and does not throw a cache delete that fails). This is the store the CLI command cannot reach (#34717's accepted limit); the server process can.
- **Wiring (`auth-plugin.ts`).** One `kernel:ready` hook, registered independently of `registerRoutes`. `kernel:ready` settles before `kernel:listening` opens the socket, so no request is served on a retired credential.
- **Fail closed.** A read or a write that does not land throws, and the boot fails with one sentence naming each account, what did not land, and the remedy (fix the database access, or `os user set-password EMAIL` first). This follows the sibling refusals, which answer `503` on a failed read and refuse a password whose stamp cannot be read, rather than accept unchecked: a server that cannot retire a seed credential does not serve while it may still act. An engine with no read surface (mock mode) or a user table that was never created holds no stamped account.
- **Idempotent.** An account retired at one boot can open no session (the `session.create.before` refusal) and mint no key (the key door requires an interactive session) before the next, so the next boot finds nothing to end.
- **Left, with the reason:** the password credential and the stamp (the refusals keep answering for them; the way out stays the operator's reset); sign-in links and one-time codes in `sys_verification` (each only opens a session, which is refused for such an account); one-time tokens (they hand over a session, which is retired); the single sign-on providers it registered and its second factor (every reset keeps them).
- **Docs.** `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx` states the rule in timeless wording and drops the release-note phrasing that named this card (round-0 nit N4 on #34717).
- **Changeset.** `.changeset/35184-dev-seed-retire-at-boot.md`: `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `!` with a BREAKING section (FROM / TO / not moved / the fix), ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, which `check-adr-0087-registration` asked for.
- **Census.** `docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts/plugins/plugin-auth.md` regenerated with `node scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs --write` (one new write call site, the reset-token delete adapter).

**Read first (by risk):**
1. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/dev-seed-credential-retirement.ts`, `retireDevSeedCredentials`: which accounts are read, the in-force filter, and the fail-closed throw.
2. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts`, the new `kernel:ready` hook: it runs on every boot outside development, including test and staging hosts.
3. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/dev-seed-credential-retirement.test.ts`, the second case (development boot) and the third (accounts whose password was set since the seed): they pin the boundary of the rule.

**Two-minute check:** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/dev-seed-credential-retirement.test.ts` shows 6 cases green.

## Tests

`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/dev-seed-credential-retirement.test.ts` (6; a real `ObjectKernel` + ObjectQL on a SQLite FILE + `AuthPlugin` with one `demoStaff` entry and the admin plugin + `SecurityPlugin`). The first boot runs in development: the seed's admin, a demo account and an administrator-created control account (no stamp) are each issued a session, an API key (written as `POST /keys` writes it) and a reset link. The server stops and boots again over the same file:

- outside development: the admin's and the demo account's sessions resolve no user, their keys answer `API_KEY_REVOKED` at the key-admission seam, their reset links are gone, each session row carries `admin_password_reset`; the control account's session, key and link are untouched; the stamp stays;
- in development: nothing is retired;
- the admin re-passworded by `setOperatorPassword` and the demo account re-passworded by the write `/admin/set-user-password` makes (stamp stale) before the boot: both untouched, and a key minted after the operator's reset is admitted;
- a second boot outside development: the tombstones are unchanged, and the retirement run once more finds the two stamped accounts and ends nothing;
- the database refusing `sys_api_key` writes: the boot fails, naming the account and `os user set-password`;
- a host `secondaryStorage` shared by both boots (the OIDC provider off, as it refuses that store): the seed accounts' sessions there are ended, the control's is kept.

## Acceptance notes

- **Which accounts, and why the narrower reading.** "Carries the development seed stamp" could mean a non-null `dev_seed_credential` column, or a stamp still in force. The code's own vocabulary ("still on the seed password is the stored hash still has this digest; any password change stops it matching") and the card's "an operator-set credential is untouched" decide it: an administrator's set-user-password leaves the column but makes it stale, and retiring on the column would end that operator-era account's sessions and keys at every restart, which also breaks idempotence. So the rule retires accounts whose seed credential is in force. Consequence, recorded: a seed-era session on an account whose password was changed in development by a door that did not revoke it (`/change-password` without `revokeOtherSessions`, or the administrator's set-user-password with its switch off) is left; the card's own words do not reach it.
- **Revoke reason.** Sessions and keys carry the existing `admin_password_reset`, the reason the operator's reset records. A dedicated reason would add an option to `sys_api_key.revoked_reason` (a `platform-objects` select, outside this card's file surface); follow-up #36313, see `## Revoke reason` below.
- **`.changeset/dev-seed-credential-production-refusal.md`** (unreleased, from #34717) is corrected in this PR, release text only: see `## DELIBERATE CORRECTION` below.
- **Test file weight.** The new file's six cases read 9.98 s of test time locally (two real boots per case); the 10 s line is close.
- The production-readiness page (`content/docs/deployment/production-readiness.mdx`) is not edited; the card names the self-hosting checklist, which now states the rule.

## DELIBERATE CORRECTION

This PR rewrites two lines in a pending release note it did not add: `.changeset/dev-seed-credential-production-refusal.md`, in the note's last paragraph. That paragraph's label and its last sentence named the boot-time retirement as something this release does not do (a follow-up). This PR ships the retirement, so left unchanged the note would publish two false lines. `check-empty-changeset` stays red by design; the dispatching seat confirms by its own record.

1. The paragraph's bold label
   - Before: "**Not ended at boot:**"
   - After: "**Ended by `os user set-password`, and at boot:**"
2. The paragraph's last sentence
   - Before: "Ending them at boot is follow-up #35184."
   - After: "In the same release, a boot outside development mode also retires them: see the note "a boot outside development mode retires what the development seed issued" (#36311)."

## Revoke reason

Retired sessions and API keys carry the existing revoke reason `admin_password_reset`, so an audit reader sees that reason, not "development seed retired". Seat 4's call (2026-11-22T05:36Z): keep it here, with no schema change in this PR. A dedicated `dev_seed_retired` value (select value, locales, field descriptions) is follow-up #36313.

- the fail-closed throw skipped: 1 red (fail-closed);
